name: Jorn van Dijk
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Framer (Amsterdam); co-runs the angel fund Festina
profile: Dutch designer with a background in graphic design and typography. With Koen Bok he co-founded Sofa, an Amsterdam studio whose Mac apps won two Apple Design Awards and which Facebook acquired in 2011; he then spent a few years designing in San Francisco. The pair launched Framer in 2014, now an AI website platform valued at $2B after a $100M Series D.
interesting_fact: Sofa, his first company with Koen Bok, made Mac apps that won two Apple Design Awards before Facebook acquired it in 2011.
deep_cut_fact: He trained in graphic design and typography rather than engineering. On his personal site he describes the past decade with Koen as 'making the internet more expressive', and through Festina they back startups in the creative space.
notes: His personal site has Notes and Videos sections, so he publishes regularly. Framer lists no press email (only support@ and abuse@).

name: Gerhard Mayr
current_role: Listed by Hurun as a founder of Aragen (role not verified)
profile: Hurun lists Gerhard Mayr as a founder of Aragen Life Sciences, the Hyderabad-based CRO/CDMO formerly known as GVK Biosciences. He does not appear on Aragen's current leadership or board page, and no public source linking him to Aragen was found. The name is shared with others, e.g. an Austrian harness-racing champion, who is unrelated.
notes: Likely Hurun attribution issue, as with Adam Richard Dawson (also listed for Aragen). Aragen's promoters are Davinder Singh Brar and Keshav Gunupati Venkat Reddy (https://www.aragen.com/leadership/). Web search budget ran out, so needs manual verification.

name: Yashwanth Kumar
profile: IIT Kharagpur alumnus who co-founded MoEngage in 2014 with CEO Raviteja Dodda. As CTO and CISO he leads technology and security for the customer engagement platform, which serves marketers in 39+ countries and is valued at about $1B. He has 15+ years building products for global enterprises.
interesting_fact: He holds both the CTO and CISO roles at MoEngage, owning engineering and information security for a platform that processes customer data for brands worldwide.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal press coverage found on MoEngage's press center. Web search budget ran out, so the research was limited.

name: Serguei Netessine
current_role: Senior Vice Dean for Innovation and Global Initiatives and Dhirubhai Ambani Professor of Innovation and Entrepreneurship, The Wharton School
profile: Moscow-educated operations and entrepreneurship scholar who worked for Motorola and Lucent before a PhD at Rochester. He taught at INSEAD (France, Singapore, Abu Dhabi) and is now a senior vice dean at Wharton. He is an angel investor, an LP in VC funds and a startup adviser, and spent about six years as an Amazon Scholar. Hurun lists him as a Thunes founder, but neither his profile nor his CV mentions Thunes.
interesting_fact: His book 'The Risk-Driven Business Model' (Harvard Business Press, 2014) won a 2015 Axiom Business Book Award, and he served on the Singapore Government's 'Future of the Economy' committee.
deep_cut_fact: He researches energy as well as entrepreneurship. He won the 2024 CEMA Best Paper Prize for 'Residential Battery Storage - Reshaping the Way We Do Electricity' and received Wharton funding for a study called 'Watts Behind the AI Revolution: Impacts of Data Centers on Energy Operations'.
notes: Strong fit for an energy and data-center podcast: his research covers grid-scale mobile batteries, renewables siting, and data-center energy use. His Thunes founder link is unverified (Thunes grew out of Singapore's TransferTo while he taught at INSEAD Singapore), so confirm before outreach. His Wharton email is published by the university.
